page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-optimized 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes 2835 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across compute and memory-intensive tasks. The server achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 20188.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 63378.89, aided by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory performance is highly competitive, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 255.6 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 104.85 GB/sec. Database operations are also a strength, with Redis SET operations reaching 67.02 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48lds_v6 offers a high-density compute profile with a reduced memory footprint, making it a cost-effective choice for workloads that require substantial processing power and local storage but do not demand massive RAM arrays. This resource balance makes it well-suited for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference, such as prompt processing with medium-sized language models.
